intent: Example Spring Boot app, example chart and a kind end-to-end test on JDK 21 and 25
Example app, example chart, kind end-to-end test and the extracted-JAR detection fix

title: recognise an extracted Spring Boot JAR as an ordinary executable JAR
why: The JAR written by -Djarmode=tools extract keeps Spring-Boot-Version but gets the application's Main-Class and a Class-Path to lib/. Treating the version attribute alone as a fat JAR made train refuse it, run tell users to extract an already extracted JAR, and fetch try to extract it again. A fat JAR keeps its dependencies in BOOT-INF, so it never has a Class-Path.
alternative: Require Start-Class or Spring-Boot-Classes — rejected: breaks fat JARs whose manifests carry only the version, and the existing fixtures

title: run the end-to-end test against a registry on the kind network, addressed by IP
why: The archive store must be reachable from pods without cluster DNS or containerd registry configuration; a registry container on the kind network is reachable by its address, and images are loaded into the node with kind load.
alternative: A registry configured through containerd patches and DNS names — rejected: more moving parts than the test needs

title: assert cache use through the JVM's own class-load log, and fallback through a JVM option changed only in the Deployment
why: Startup time is noisy on a shared machine; the application class's load source ('shared objects file' versus the JAR) is exact. A relevant option such as -Xmx added only to the Deployment's command leaves fetch's fingerprint matching but makes run reject the archive, which is the realistic way a team breaks it.

name: example app
role: A Spring Boot 3.5 web app extracted at image build time, used by the example chart and the kind test
conditions: One image per JDK (--build-arg JDK); compiled for 21

name: example-app chart
role: A workload chart using mnemo-warmup as an aliased dependency and its pod-template helpers
conditions: warmup.app.jvmArgs feeds the trainer, fetch and the Deployment's command so they agree; javaOptions is for options that do not matter to an archive

subject: dependency:go-offline
why: It failed after almost four minutes for the Spring Boot plugin; a BuildKit cache mount on ~/.m2 caches just as well

subject: Extracted Spring Boot manifest
why: Spring-Boot-Version survives extraction, so the version attribute cannot identify a fat JAR

subject: Real Spring Boot was never exercised before
why: Earlier tests used tiny plain JARs, which hid the detection problem
